dedupe_keys.name: geoscience australia earthquake scenario selection tool

description: The Earthquake Scenario Selection tool from Geoscience Australia lets users query, visualise and download pre-generated earthquake scenarios for more than 160 sites around Australia. Each scenario represents a plausible future earthquake, and the stated purpose is emergency management and planning, for example preparing response exercises or estimating what a moderate to large local earthquake would mean for a town. The producer is Geoscience Australia for the Commonwealth of Australia, linked to its National Seismic Hazard Assessment work. Coverage is national, site by site. The tool sits in the hazards view of the Geoscience Australia portal and is described by a metadata record created in June 2021 and updated in August 2025; the data are released under CC BY 4.0 and are free to use. Caveats: the portal is an interactive map application, so formats and variables of the downloads could not be read here and should be checked in the portal; scenarios are hypothetical, and the record does not describe damage or loss estimates, only the scenarios themselves. Simulation uses: ground motion inputs for exercises and for exposure of hospitals, emergency facilities and lifelines in Australian cities. Related records: the USGS ShakeMap scenario catalogs (data-usgs-shakemap-scenario-catalog) and Canada's National Earthquake Scenario Catalogue (data-canada-national-earthquake-scenario-catalogue) serve the same planning role.
